Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
53-y/o male with 1-week painless swelling and warmth over left olecranon; likely olecranon bursitis. Started on NSAID and blood tests arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Painless swelling over left elbow noticed ~1 week ago; feels warm, mild tenderness adjacent to tip, full movement preserved.  
• No trauma, no prior episodes, no occupational overuse (desk job).  
• Associated symptoms: denies systemic illness; no other joint involvement noted.  
• Past medical history: Osteoarthritis (diagnosed by GP several years ago); peanut allergy. No other chronic illnesses.  
• Medications: None routinely.  
• Drug allergies: None known.  
• Social: Works at a desk; runs 2–3×/week. Non-contributory history of alcohol/smoking not covered. Preventive care not discussed.

Examination:
• Vitals: not documented.  
• Video inspection: Visible swelling over left olecranon; skin slightly warm; mild focal tenderness lateral to tip; skin at tip appears dry; full active range of motion.

Impression:
• Probable olecranon bursitis (non-septic).  
• Septic arthritis considered unlikely but safety-net advice given.

Plan:
• Start ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily with food (OTC) – stop if heartburn.  
• Arrange blood tests: inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, uric acid (gout). Test forms to be mailed to patient.  
• Follow-up: patient to book review (video or face-to-face) ~6 days after blood draw to assess elbow and review results.  
• Safety net: Seek urgent medical review if elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, or redness spreads (concern for septic arthritis).  

Quality checks:

● Expected elements missing: vitals, medication reconciliation beyond “none,” surgical history, smoking/alcohol status, immunization history.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript clear overall; minor inaudible/elliptical phrases but core clinical content intact.
